leftEvidence.title: Absalom forces a meeting with Joab and the king

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Absalom’s appearance and children are named; after two years without seeing David he sends for Joab, burns Joab’s field when ignored, and finally bows before the king, who kisses him.
points.right: At the season when kings go out, David remains in Jerusalem, sees a woman bathing, asks who she is, sends messengers, takes her, and receives word of pregnancy.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a kiss closes the chapter without explaining whether the household breach is repaired inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places royal distance from battle concentrates action in the king’s verbs inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 14:25–33 and 2 Samuel 11:1–5 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Taking, Rebuke, and House Fracture” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: The king remains, sees, sends, and takes

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 14:25–33 foregrounds a kiss closes the chapter without explaining whether the household breach is repaired; 2 Samuel 11:1–5 foregrounds royal distance from battle concentrates action in the king’s verbs. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
